To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a new estimator has been developed for estimating the period of periodic point processes from sparse, noisy observations.
the proposed estimator is statistically superior to the existing estimators, and has a computational complexity that is comparable to that of the best of the existing estimators.
a) we propose a new method of maximum likelihood estimation for the period of periodic point processes that is computationally efficient and b) we prove that the method is statistically consistent.
In summary, our research is concerned with
estimating the period of an unknown periodic point process from a set of observations.
the problem of estimating the fundamental period of a point process from sparse, noisy observations.

the problem of estimating the periodicity of a signal from a sparse and noisy set of observations, which is a problem that is relevant to many areas of signal processing and communications, and is also of fundamental importance in statistics.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the proposed algorithm is the most accurate and efficient method for period estimation from noisy timing data, with an expected arithmetic complexity of O(n3 log(n)), where n is the size of the data set.

, for the statistical model and numerical implementation considered here, the maximum- likelihood estimator outperforms all other estimators in terms of both statistical accuracy and computational efficiency.
the new estimator is the best one in the class of estimators operating by maximizing an objective over a sampled interval of possible periods.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the new method provides a statistically accurate estimate of the period of a sparse and noisy periodic point process with a computational complexity that is comparable to that of the line-search algorithms.

we have proposed a new estimator which is statistically more accurate than the estimators of Fogel & Gavish, Sidiropoulos, et al., and Clarkson, and which has lower arithmetic complexity than the estimator of Clarkson.
we provide a maximum-likelihood period estimation algorithm for sparse, noisy timing observations.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, when the observations are noisy, the sampling of the period interval should be as dense as possible.
the maximum-likelihood approach to period estimation is feasible for sparse data.
, in many cases, the maximum-likelihood periodogram is a more statistically robust estimator than the periodogram estimator.
